literal: Reaching the end of the Zhengguang era, wicked parasites seized power; that government was largely perverse, and the nine domains were torn apart.
idiomatic: By the end of the Zhengguang era wicked men had seized power; government turned corrupt, and the realm was torn apart.

literal: Yongan saw its mandate exhausted; men and spirits were destroyed and wasted; rebel hosts filled the sky, carving up the four seas—state and land, subjects and people, no longer seemed to belong to Wei.
idiomatic: Under Yongan the mandate ran out; men and spirits withered; rebels rose everywhere and carved up the empire—land and people no longer seemed Wei's own.

literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi seized the timely moment, rising like a phoenix and soaring like a dragon; he raised the fallen to establish Heaven, set propping pillars to steady the earth, cut down and extinguished the people's poison, righted our fallen calendar, bore great virtue toward the Wei house, and spread broad benefit upon the black-haired people.
idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi took up the moment—rising like a phoenix, soaring like a dragon—raised the fallen throne, shored up the realm, uprooted the poison of chaos, and restored our broken calendar; great was his merit to Wei, wide his blessing to the people.

literal: When Wenxiang succeeded the track, he brought forth light to the former enterprise: within he exterminated fierce power; without he shattered invading rebellion; far and near grew orderly and tranquil; his merit reached to High Dark Heaven.
idiomatic: When Wenxiang followed after, he carried the earlier work forward—crushing traitors within, breaking invaders without—until far and near grew quiet and his merit reached heaven.

literal: Your Majesty's spirit and the deities accord in virtue; you are boat and bridge for an age; your form is literary brilliance and martial display; you pursue change and exhaust the subtle.
idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue aligns with heaven and earth; you are the bridge of an age, embodying civil splendor and martial might, probing change to its roots.

literal: From your first footsteps at the frontier banner, songs of praise gathered all; entering to preside over the pivot-mechanism, your wind-teaching is vast and far.
idiomatic: From your first days at the frontier banner, praise gathered everywhere; once you took the helm, your governance grew broad and far-reaching.

literal: Having greatly inherited the worldly enterprise, upholding the state and prospering the family, your assisting virtue daily ascends; hegemonic wind grows ever loftier; when authority and spirit are thus unimpeded, the wild and distant come as guests; where renown and strategy spread, neighboring foes submit in good faith.
idiomatic: Having inherited the great enterprise, you upheld the state and prospered the house—your virtue rising day by day, your hegemony spreading ever wider. Where your authority reaches, the distant come as guests; where your name travels, neighboring foes offer submission.

literal: With the resource of wealth, wielding extraordinary spirit, in the blink of an eye none who think of it fail to submit.
idiomatic: With boundless resources and a singular spirit, in a single glance none fail to submit.

literal: Secret tokens lie hidden within; a thousand sacrifices make them clear; auspicious portents once dark and secret in one morning pour forth in array—to show the season for dynastic virtue, to open the track of rising state; Dark Dark Above gazes near, not far to shine upon.
idiomatic: Hidden tokens long concealed now shine clear through a thousand rites; secret auspices pour forth in a single morning—to mark the hour when virtue changes hands and a new state rises. Heaven above looks down from no great distance.

literal: I, being empty and dim, still have not hesitated and withdrawn; quiet words bring shame; I sit awaiting dawn.
idiomatic: I am unworthy and still have not withdrawn; even in silence I feel shame, sitting through the night until dawn.

literal: Moreover when the time comes fate goes; Gui and Shun had no leisure to face south; when the world changed and the mandate turned, Bo Yu could not remain facing north—how much less one so meager and thin, who could dawdle!
idiomatic: When the time comes, fate moves on—Emperors Gui and Shun could not linger on the throne; when the world changed, Yu could not remain in the north facing south. How much less can one as unworthy as I hesitate and delay!

literal: Therefore looking up to accord with vaulted Heaven, looking down to follow the hundred surnames, I reverently with formula confer the imperial seat upon Your Majesty the King.
idiomatic: Therefore I look up to heaven and down to the people, and solemnly confer the throne upon you, my king.

literal: Heaven's blessing ends forever; the great mandate has arrived.
idiomatic: Heaven's blessing is at an end; the great mandate has passed.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: Reverently receive the sequence of fate, truly hold the center, respond to and raise Heaven's favor—may this reign be ten thousand years—how could it not be glorious!
idiomatic: Reverently accept the mandate, hold fast to the mean, and answer heaven's grace—may your reign endure ten thousand years! What glory could surpass this!

literal: He also sent a seal-letter to the Emperor, dispatching Acting Grand Mentor Prince of Pengcheng Gao Shao and Acting Minister of Works Jing Xianjun to deliver the imperial seal and cord; the abdication rite followed entirely the precedents of Tang-Yao, Han, and Wei.
idiomatic: He also sent a sealed letter to the emperor, dispatching Acting Grand Mentor Prince Pengcheng Gao Shao and Acting Minister of Works Jing Xianjun to present the imperial seal and cord; the abdication followed the ancient precedents of Yao, of Han, and of Wei.

literal: Also Minister of Works Chief Gao Longzhi led the hundred officials in urging advancement.
idiomatic: Minister of Works Chief Gao Longzhi also led the hundred officials in urging Gao Yang to accept the throne.

literal: On wuwu, he thereupon ascended the imperial seat at the Southern Altar; mounting the altar with fagot-fire sacrifice he addressed Heaven, saying:
idiomatic: On wuwu Gao Yang ascended the throne at the Southern Altar; mounting the altar and kindling the sacrificial fire, he addressed Heaven:

literal: The Emperor, subject Yang, dares with black bull to clearly announce to August August Emperors and Empresses: adversity and ease follow in succession; abolition and rise alternate in use; the utmost Way is without partiality—when fate responds, one assists it.
idiomatic: I, Yang, your subject, dare with a black bull to proclaim before the Lord on High and the Earth: fortune and ruin succeed each other; thrones rise and fall in turn; the Way shows no favor—it aids those whom fate chooses.

literal: Looking up I examine Tang and Yu; looking down I trace Wei and Jin—none failed to first yield by bow in Heaven's command, examining the calendar until return was complete.
idiomatic: From Yao and Shun above to Wei and Jin below, none failed to yield the throne when heaven decreed it, until the mandate ran its course.

literal: The Wei house had many troubles; the years nearly thirty; after Xiaochang, within and without abandoned it.
idiomatic: Wei suffered calamity after calamity for nearly thirty years; after Xiaochang, court and realm alike turned from it.

literal: The world's way flowed crosswise; the black-haired people were smeared on the roasting-block.
idiomatic: The age ran wild; the people burned on the roasting-block of war.

literal: Relying on our Founding Wu, he rescued those about to drown; thrice he established chief heads, twice he re-established the ancestral temple; he swept away all villain bands and mowed down treacherous scoundrels.
idiomatic: Thanks to our Founding Ancestor, the drowning were pulled back—thrice he raised a ruler, twice he restored the ancestral line, sweeping away gangs of villains and cutting down traitors.

literal: Virtue spread to black-headed masses; merit lit the universe.
idiomatic: His virtue covered the people; his merit lit the universe.

literal: Wenxiang continued the martial track, able to construct the great foundation; merit soaked through the realm; authority overawed beyond the seas; those with hair to the roots held good faith; western bandits submitted; Blue Mound kept frontier guard; Cinnabar Cave came to court; he assisted at the crisis, again righted the falling fortune—this was great creation for the Wei house.
idiomatic: Wenxiang followed in his footsteps and built the great foundation—merit filling the realm, authority reaching beyond the seas, distant lands keeping faith, western foes submitting, frontier tribes sending tribute. He steadied Wei in its crisis and righted its falling fortune—great indeed was his service to Wei.

literal: The Wei Emperor, because divination showed the era ending, Upper Spirits weary of virtue, reverently as to August Heaven, truly returned the great mandate, abdicating to subject Yang.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor, seeing that his dynasty's span was ending and heaven had turned from Wei, reverently acknowledged that the mandate belonged elsewhere and abdicated to me, Yang.

literal: The four seas are utmost fairness; all under heaven are one; overseeing the people and governing the age requires setting a lord upon them—since rivers and mountains opened their tokens and men and spirits presented blessings, dukes, ministers, and gentry, the eight directions' myriad multitudes all say the imperial pole now looks above, and Wei pushes advancement below—the heavenly seat cannot for a moment stand empty.
idiomatic: The four seas belong to all; the realm is one—ruling the people requires a sovereign. Rivers and mountains have shown their signs; men and spirits have blessed the change. Lords and ministers and the people of every land say heaven's gaze has turned upward while Wei yields from below—the throne cannot stand empty even for a day.

literal: Thus pressed by massed counsel, I reverently received the great ceremony.
idiomatic: Pressed by the unanimous will of all, I reverently accept the great rite.

literal: Meanly with meager thinness, entrusted above the myriad multitudes—though Heaven's majesty is on my face and no distance within arm's reach, examining myself in reflection I truly harbor reverent fear.
idiomatic: Unworthy as I am, I am placed above the people—though heaven's majesty is upon my brow and no distance is far from my reach, looking within myself I feel only reverence and dread.

literal: Reverently selecting the primordial day, mounting the altar to receive abdication, broadly classifying God Above, to answer the hearts of ten thousand states—forever elevating auspicious blessings, protecting and aiding You Qi, to extend to endless fortune.
idiomatic: On this sacred day I mount the altar to receive the abdication and worship God above, to answer the hearts of all lands—may blessings flourish forever, may Qi be protected and its fortune extend without end.

literal: That day the capital obtained a red sparrow and presented it at the Southern Altar.
idiomatic: That day a red sparrow was caught in the capital and presented at the Southern Altar.

literal: When the affair was done, he returned to the palace and held court at the Front Hall of Grand Ultimate.
idiomatic: When the rites were finished, he returned to the palace and took his seat at the Front Hall of the Grand Ultimate.

literal: An edict said: "Having no virtue yet bearing the name, replacing punishment with rites; not speaking yet trusted, putting spring before autumn.
idiomatic: An edict said: "To bear the name without merit is to govern by ritual rather than punishment; to win trust without words is to put nurture before severity.

literal: Thus one knows that compassionate transformation makes Heaven and men one measure; the way of broad pardon is the same wind in ancient and modern times.
idiomatic: Compassion links heaven and earth; mercy has been the same wind in every age.

literal: I, being empty and thin, have no record of achievement in merit-work.
idiomatic: I am unworthy, my achievements without measure.

literal: Formerly the Founding Xianwu Wang met Wei's unlucky times; the nine cauldrons wandered forth; he thereupon drove and commanded the feudal lords, raised the great name of Yan and Zhao, rescued their about-to-fall, causing the perished thus to exist.
idiomatic: In Wei's evil hour our Founding Ancestor took up arms when the realm was lost, called the lords of Yan and Zhao to his banner, and snatched the falling dynasty from ruin, making the dead live again.

literal: Prince Wenxiang outwardly thrust martial achievement, inwardly endowed with bright virtue; he inherited the martial track of the former enterprise, opened territory and brought the distant to submission.
idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang displayed martial prowess abroad and bright virtue at home, inheriting the martial enterprise and opening lands until distant peoples submitted.

literal: Years passed more than two decades; generations crossed two capitals; prison lawsuits had their proper place; songs of praise were there.
idiomatic: For more than twenty years, through two capitals, lawsuits were justly judged and songs of praise were heard.

literal: Therefore the Wei Emperor bowed to follow the calendar sequence, thereupon thinking of lifting robe, far taking Tang and Yu, finally the same as casting off shoes.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor therefore bowed to heaven's decree, thinking to lift his robe and go—as Yao and Yu did before him—casting off the throne like an old shoe.

literal: Truly hidden sorrow was not yet ended; his will was at Yangcheng—yet the massed dukes, ministers, and gentry, sincere in guardianship ever more pressing, thereupon entrusted the succession's end; dwelling above the people is like wading deep water, anxious through the whole morning.
idiomatic: His heart still grieved and his wish was to withdraw to Yangcheng, but lords and ministers pressed ever more urgently; the mandate had passed and the throne could not stand empty. To reign over the people is to wade deep water—I feel that anxiety every morning.

literal: From first setting out from Jinyang, the nine-tailed fox presented auspice; at the outer altar heaven was addressed; the red sparrow showed blessing.
idiomatic: From the day we set out from Jinyang, a nine-tailed fox appeared as an omen; at the altar we addressed heaven, and the red sparrow brought its blessing.

literal: You alone, civil and military ministers of undivided heart, arm-and-thigh and claw-and-tooth generals, who aided the former kings and jointly grandly built the great enterprise—forever speak sincere loyalty, together sharing this restful blessing.
idiomatic: You civil and military ministers of loyal heart, you generals who were arm and claw to our former kings—you helped build this great work. May your loyalty endure, and may you share in these blessings.

literal: Thinking to with the hundred million begin together on this day—there shall be a grand amnesty throughout the realm.
idiomatic: On this day I would begin anew with all my people—a general amnesty is proclaimed throughout the realm.

literal: Change Wuding year eight to Tianbao year one.
idiomatic: Wuding year eight is changed to Tianbao year one.

literal: Officials shall advance in rank; men shall be granted nobility; widowers, widows, the six afflictions, righteous husbands and chaste wives—commendation and reward each with differences."
idiomatic: Officials are promoted in rank; common men are granted nobility; widows, orphans, the disabled, worthy husbands and chaste wives—all are honored and rewarded according to merit."

literal: On jiwei, an edict enfeoffed the Wei Emperor as Prince of Zhongshan, fief of ten thousand households; in memorials he need not call himself subject, in replies no "edict" is used; he bears the Son of Heaven's banners, follows Wei's calendar, rides the five-seasons secondary carriage;
idiomatic: On jiwei an edict enfeoffed the former Wei emperor as Prince of Zhongshan with a fief of ten thousand households; his memorials need not call him subject, nor would replies be styled as edicts; he would bear imperial banners, keep Wei's calendar, and ride the secondary chariot of the five seasons;

literal: his sons were enfeoffed as district dukes, fiefs of a thousand households;
idiomatic: his sons were enfeoffed as district dukes with fiefs of one thousand households;

literal: he was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, ten million cash, twenty thousand piculs of grain, two hundred slaves, one water mill, a hundred qing of fields, and one garden estate.
idiomatic: and he was granted ten thousand bolts of silk, ten million cash, twenty thousand piculs of grain, two hundred slaves, one water mill, a hundred qing of land, and an estate garden.

literal: An edict posthumously honored the imperial grandfather Prince Wenmu as Emperor Wenmu, his consort as Empress Wenmu, the imperial father Prince Xianwu as Emperor Xianwu, the imperial elder brother Prince Wenxiang as Emperor Wenxiang; titles for the ancestors—entrust to outer offices for rapid deliberation and report.
idiomatic: An edict posthumously honored his grandfather as Emperor Wenmu and his grandmother as Empress Wenmu, his father as Emperor Xianwu, and his elder brother as Emperor Wenxiang; ancestral temple titles were referred to the outer offices for prompt deliberation and report.

literal: On xinyou, the Queen Mother was honored as Empress Dowager.
idiomatic: On xinyou the queen mother was honored as empress dowager.

literal: On yichou, an edict lowered Wei-dynasty enfeoffments and ranks, each with differences.
idiomatic: On yichou an edict reduced the titles and ranks of the former Wei court, each according to rank.

literal: Those of Xindu who followed righteousness and those who declared strength for the hegemonic court, and those who came from the west, and all who since Wuding year six came south to submit and transform—are not within the reduction limit.
idiomatic: Those of Xindu who had kept faith, those who had served the Gao cause, arrivals from the west, and all who since Wuding year six had come south to submit were exempt from the reduction.

literal: On xinwei, envoys were dispatched to the four directions to observe customs, inquire into people's hardships, strictly admonish district officials, urge them with integrity and fairness, promote benefit and remove harm, striving to preserve tranquility.
idiomatic: On xinwei he sent envoys to every quarter to observe local customs, inquire into the people's hardships, and strictly admonish officials to govern with integrity, promote what benefits the people, remove what harms them, and keep the realm at peace.

literal: If law has what is inconvenient to the time, or government has what is not exhaustive for affairs, fully itemize gain and loss and return to the capital to report.
idiomatic: Where laws no longer fit the times or policies fall short, they were to itemize strengths and flaws and report back to the capital.

literal: On jiaxu, the spirit tablets were moved to the Grand Temple.
idiomatic: On jiaxu the ancestral tablets were moved to the Grand Temple.

literal: On jimao of the sixth month, Goguryeo sent envoys in court tribute.
idiomatic: On jimao of the sixth month, Goguryeo sent envoys with tribute.

literal: On xinsi, an edict said: "Recently customs drift and float; vain rivalry daily grows; when families have fortune or misfortune, they strive to outdo in strangeness.
idiomatic: On xinsi an edict said: "Customs have grown loose and rivalry extravagant; in weddings and funerals every household strives to outdo the rest.

literal: Expenses for marriage and funeral, splendor of carriage-robes, drink, and food—moving to exhaust a year's resources to scheme for daily wealth.
idiomatic: The cost of marriages and funerals, the finery of carriage and dress, the luxury of food and wine—yearly income is poured out to flaunt daily wealth.

literal: Moreover slaves wore gold and jade; maidservants wore gauze and brocade—at first taking innovation as marvel, later taking surpassing predecessors as beauty; high and low, noble and base, again had no gradation of difference.
idiomatic: Slaves wear gold and jade; maidservants wear silk and brocade—first novelty became fashion, then surpassing the last became the rule, until high and low knew no distinction.

literal: Now fate belongs to renewal alone; thinking to wipe away former abuses, returning to simplicity and restoring purity, bringing the people within compass and things.
idiomatic: Now that the mandate is renewed, we would wipe away old abuses, restore simplicity, and bring the people back within proper bounds.

literal: According to circumstances fully establish articles and forms, making thrift yet obtain the mean.
idiomatic: Let regulations be drawn up as the times require, so that thrift may hold the mean."

literal: Also an edict enfeoffed Lord Honored Sage with a fief of a hundred households to maintain sacrifice to Confucius, and ordered Lu Commandery timely to repair and maintain temple halls, striving to exhaust utmost praise and honor.
idiomatic: Another edict enfeoffed Lord Honored Sage with a fief of one hundred households to maintain sacrifices to Confucius, and ordered Lu Commandery to repair the temple in due season with all due reverence.

literal: An edict dispatched envoys separately to perform sacrifice at the Five Peaks and Four Rivers; the shrines of Yao and temples of Shun, down to Kong Fu, Lord Lao, and others recorded in the sacrificial canon—all received rites without omission.
idiomatic: Envoys were sent to offer sacrifice at the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Rivers; shrines to Yao and Shun, Kong Fu, Lord Lao, and all others in the sacrificial canon received rites without omission.

literal: An edict said: "The two commanderies of Bohai and Changle in Ji Province were the Former Emperor's first enfeoffment, the place where the righteousness-banner first rose.
idiomatic: An edict said: "The commanderies of Bohai and Changle in Ji Province were our Founding Ancestor's first fief and the place where the banner of revolt first rose.

literal: Taiyuan in Bing Province and Qi Commandery in Qing Province—where the hegemonic enterprise dwelt, where the kingly mandate was foundation.
idiomatic: Taiyuan in Bing Province and Qi Commandery in Qing Province were the seat of our enterprise and the foundation of our mandate.

literal: When a gentleman has accomplishment, he honors not forgetting roots; thinking to extend grace and reach, remission and restoration of land tax.
idiomatic: A worthy man, when he achieves, does not forget his roots; thinking to extend grace to the land, we remit the land tax.

literal: Qi Commandery and Bohai may together be remitted one year; Changle remitted two years; Taiyuan remitted three years."
idiomatic: Qi and Bohai are remitted one year, Changle two years, Taiyuan three years."

literal: An edict: Former Grand Tutor Sun Teng, Former Grand Mentor Wei Jing, Former Grand Marshal Lou Zhao, Former Minister of Works Gao Ang, Former Left Vice Minister of Works Murong Shaozong, Former Army Commander Wanqigan, Former Inspector of Dingzhou Duan Rong, Former Palace Censor Liu Gui, Former Palace Censor Dou Tai, Former Inspector of Yinzhou Liu Feng, Former Inspector of Jizhou Cai Jun and others—all aided the former emperors and managed the imperial foundation; some unfortunately died early, some perished in royal service—envoys may be sent to their tombs to perform sacrifice, and also comfort and inquire after wives and children, extending solace to the living and the dead.
idiomatic: An edict ordered sacrifice at the tombs of the late Sun Teng, Wei Jing, Lou Zhao, Gao Ang, Murong Shaozong, Wanqigan, Duan Rong, Liu Gui, Dou Tai, Liu Feng, Cai Jun, and others who had served the former emperors and built the dynasty—some dying early, some falling in the state's service—and directed that their wives and children be comforted, extending solace to living and dead.

literal: Also an edict enfeoffed clan members Gao Yue as Prince of Qinghe, Gao Longzhi as Prince of Pingyuan, Gao Guiyan as Prince of Pingqin, Gao Sizong as Prince of Shangluo, Gao Changbi as Prince of Guangwu, Gao Pu as Prince of Wuxing, Gao Ziyuan as Prince of Pingchang, Gao Xianguo as Prince of Xiangle, Gao Rui as Prince of Zhaojun, Gao Xiaoxu as Prince of Xiucheng.
idiomatic: Another edict enfeoffed Gao Yue as Prince of Qinghe, Gao Longzhi as Prince of Pingyuan, Gao Guiyan as Prince of Pingqin, Gao Sizong as Prince of Shangluo, Gao Changbi as Prince of Guangwu, Gao Pu as Prince of Wuxing, Gao Ziyuan as Prince of Pingchang, Gao Xianguo as Prince of Xiangle, Gao Rui as Prince of Zhaojun, and Gao Xiaoxu as Prince of Xiucheng.

literal: Also an edict enfeoffed meritorious ministers Kudi Gan as Prince of Zhangwu, Helü Jin as Prince of Xianyang, Heba Ren as Prince of Anding, Han Gui as Prince of Ande, Kezhuhun Daoyuan as Prince of Fufeng, Peng Yue as Prince of Chenliu, Pan Xiangle as Prince of Hedong.
idiomatic: Meritorious ministers were enfeoffed: Kudi Gan as Prince of Zhangwu, Helü Jin as Prince of Xianyang, Heba Ren as Prince of Anding, Han Gui as Prince of Ande, Kezhuhun Daoyuan as Prince of Fufeng, Peng Yue as Prince of Chenliu, and Pan Xiangle as Prince of Hedong.

literal: On guim wei, an edict enfeoffed younger brothers: Qingzhou Inspector Gao Jun as Prince of Yong'an, Left Vice Minister Gao Yan as Prince of Pingyang, Dingzhou Inspector Gao You as Prince of Pengcheng, Opening-Fu Third Rank Gao Yan as Prince of Changshan, Jizhou Inspector Gao Huan as Prince of Shangdang, Opening-Fu Third Rank Gao Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng, Opening-Fu Third Rank Gao Zhan as Prince of Ch'angguang, Gao Jie as Prince of Rencheng, Gao Shi as Prince of Gaoyang, Gao Ji as Prince of Boling, Gao Ning as Prince of Xinping, Gao Run as Prince of Fengyi, Gao Qia as Prince of Hanyang.
idiomatic: On guim wei younger brothers were enfeoffed: Gao Jun, Qingzhou inspector, as Prince of Yong'an; Gao Yan, Left Vice Minister, as Prince of Pingyang; Gao You, Dingzhou inspector, as Prince of Pengcheng; Gao Yan, Opening-Fu Third Rank, as Prince of Changshan; Gao Huan, Jizhou inspector, as Prince of Shangdang; Gao Yu as Prince of Xiangcheng; Gao Zhan as Prince of Ch'angguang; Gao Jie as Prince of Rencheng; Gao Shi as Prince of Gaoyang; Gao Ji as Prince of Boling; Gao Ning as Prince of Xinping; Gao Run as Prince of Fengyi; and Gao Qia as Prince of Hanyang.

literal: On dinghai, an edict established Prince Yin as Crown Prince, Queen Li as Empress.
idiomatic: On dinghai an edict established Prince Yin as crown prince and Lady Li as empress.

literal: On gengyin, an edict appointed Grand Preceptor Kudi Gan as Grand Mentor, Minister of Works Peng Yue as Grand Marshal, Minister of Education Pan Xiangle as Minister of Works, Opening-Fu Third Rank Sima Ziru as Minister of Education.
idiomatic: On gengyin an edict appointed Grand Preceptor Kudi Gan as Grand Mentor, Minister of Works Peng Yue as Grand Marshal, Minister of Education Pan Xiangle as Minister of Works, and Opening-Fu Third Rank Sima Ziru as Minister of Education.

literal: On xinmao, former Grand Marshal Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue was made Bearer of the Staff, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Inspector of Sizhou.
idiomatic: On xinmao former Grand Marshal Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue was made Bearer of the Staff, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Inspector of Sizhou.

literal: On renchen, an edict said: "From now on, all who have written memorials discussing affairs and stating essentials and secrets—the responsible offices shall all memorialize and report.
idiomatic: On renchen an edict said: "From this day forward, all memorials discussing affairs and stating matters of importance or secrecy shall be forwarded and reported by the responsible offices.

literal: On jihai, because the Crown Prince first entered the Eastern Palace, amnesty within the capital precincts and Bing Province for death crimes and below; in other provinces death reduced, exile and penal servitude and below all pardoned and exempted.
idiomatic: On jihai, because the crown prince first entered the Eastern Palace, death sentences and below were pardoned within the capital precincts and Bing Province; in other provinces death was commuted and exile and penal servitude and below were all remitted.

literal: Autumn, seventh month, xinhai—an edict honored Wenxiang's consort Lady Yuan as Empress Wenxiang, palace named Jingde.
idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on xinhai, an edict honored Wenxiang's consort Lady Yuan as Empress Wenxiang, with her palace named Jingde.

literal: Also enfeoffed Wenxiang Emperor's sons Xiaowan as Prince of Hejian, Xiaoyu as Prince of Henan.
idiomatic: Gao Yang also enfeoffed Wenxiang's sons Xiaowan as Prince of Hejian and Xiaoyu as Prince of Henan.

literal: On yimao, Minister of Works Chief Pingyuan Wang Longzhi recorded Masters of Writing affairs; Left Vice Minister Pingyang Wang Yan became Minister of Works Chief.
idiomatic: On yimao Minister of Works Chief Prince of Pingyuan Gao Longzhi was ordered to record Masters of Writing affairs, and Left Vice Minister Prince of Pingyang Gao Yan became Minister of Works Chief.

literal: Also an edict: "Ancient men used deerskin for robes, book bags for curtains—having hearts of great virtue, their elegance can be imagined.
idiomatic: Another edict said: "Ancient men wore deerskin and kept books in leather bags—men of great virtue whose elegance we can still imagine.

literal: The Wei imperial treasury's rare and strange assorted colors usually not given to people—merely stored in accumulation—command that all should be taken out, sent to the inner rear garden, to supply the seven-day feast and bestowal."
idiomatic: The Wei imperial treasury holds rare treasures and fine silks never given away—they lie hoarded in store. Let them all be brought out to the inner rear garden for the seven-day feast and distribution."

literal: Eighth month, edict for commanderies and states to repair and establish schools, broadly extend talented youths, earnestly continue Confucian wind.
idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict ordered the commanderies and principalities to repair schools, recruit talented youths, and revive Confucian learning.

literal: National University students also depend on old standards for selection and appointment, embrace masters' teachings, study the Classic of Rites.
idiomatic: National University students were also to be selected and appointed by the old standards, follow their teachers' instruction, and study the Classic of Rites.

literal: Formerly Wenxiang Emperor's transported Cai Yong stone classics fifty-two tablets—immediately should be moved and placed in the academy, sequentially repaired and established.
idiomatic: The fifty-two stone classic tablets of Cai Yong that Wenxiang had transported were to be moved at once to the academy and set up in proper order.

literal: Also an edict: "Those able to speak straight and remonstrate rightly, not avoiding guilt—urgent as Zhu Yun, blunt as Zhou She—opening my thought, watering my heart, assisting the One Person, benefiting the hundred surnames—shall surely be favored with glory and salary, treated with exceptional promotion.
idiomatic: Another edict said: "Whoever speaks straight and remonstrates without fear of punishment—bold as Zhu Yun, blunt as Zhou She—opening my mind and aiding my rule to the people's benefit shall be honored with rank and salary and advanced without regard to precedent.

literal: Also said: "All officials who shepherd the people should dedicatedly focus on farming and silkworms, diligently encourage assessment, broadly gather heaven-and-earth's profit, to prepare for flood and drought calamities.
idiomatic: It also said: "All officials who govern the people must devote themselves to farming and sericulture, encourage the harvest, gather the land's bounty, and prepare against flood and drought.

literal: Gengyin, edict: "I with empty widowhood succeed the vast kingly enterprise, thinking how to praise and raise glorious achievement, spreading it to ten thousand ancients.
idiomatic: On gengyin an edict said: "Unworthy as I am, I have inherited the great enterprise and wish to praise its achievements and spread them to posterity.

literal: Although historiographers hold the brush, what is heard is not lost—still fearing stray words leave beauty behind, sometimes not yet written.
idiomatic: Though the historiographers record what they hear, I fear that fine words may still be lost and deeds left unwritten.

literal: Those in office—kings, dukes, civil and military great and small—descending to the common multitudes, even to monk disciples—whether personally receiving verbal commands or receiving transmitted side-talk—all writable documents should be fully itemized, recorded, and sealed upward.
idiomatic: Princes and officials, civil and military, down to commoners and even monks—whether they heard commands directly or by report—should submit in full whatever written records can be made."

literal: Jiawu, edict: "Wei times deliberated and fixed the Linzhi Code, thus making common regulation; official offices applied it—still not entirely good.
idiomatic: On jiawu an edict said: "Wei deliberated and fixed the Linzhi Code as the general law, yet in practice it is still not wholly satisfactory.

literal: May command the massed officials further to add deliberation and investigation.
idiomatic: Let the officials deliberate further upon it.

literal: Appropriate governing methods—first exhaust what is essential and urgent.
idiomatic: In reforming the law, begin with what is most essential and urgent.

literal: Leading the net to order the items—must make nothing omitted."
idiomatic: Set out the main principles and arrange the details, and let nothing be left out."

literal: On guichou of the ninth month, made Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Flying Cavalry Grand General, Director of Eastern Yi, Liaodong Commandery Founding Duke, Goguryeo King Seong as Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Flying Cavalry Grand General, Director Protecting Eastern Yi—king and duke as before.
idiomatic: On guichou of the ninth month Goguryeo King Seong, already Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Flying Cavalry Grand General, Director of Eastern Yi, and Founding Duke of Liaodong Commandery, was further made Bearer of the Staff, Attendant-in-Ordinary, Flying Cavalry Grand General, and Director Protecting Eastern Yi—his royal and ducal titles unchanged.

literal: An edict made Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bearer of Staff, Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Director of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Acting-by-Edict, Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun as Prince of Liang.
idiomatic: An edict enfeoffed Liang Attendant-in-Ordinary, Bearer of the Staff, Acting Yellow Battle-Axe, Director of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Grand General, Acting-by-Edict, Prince of Shaoling Xiao Lun as Prince of Liang.

literal: Gengwu, the Emperor went to Jinyang, bowing farewell at the mountain tombs.
idiomatic: On gengwu the emperor went to Jinyang and bowed farewell at the mountain tombs.

literal: That day the Crown Prince entered and dwelt at Cool Breeze Hall, overseeing and summing state affairs.
idiomatic: That day the crown prince took up residence at Cool Breeze Hall and oversaw state affairs.

literal: Winter, tenth month, jimao, equipped with law chariot, rode the golden carriage, entered Jinyang Palace, attended the Empress Dowager at the inner hall.
idiomatic: On jimao of the tenth month of winter, with full imperial escort he rode the golden carriage into Jinyang Palace and attended the empress dowager in the inner hall.

literal: Xinsi, partial amnesty for Bingzhou Taiyuan Commandery Jinyang County and the Chancellor's Office four prisons' prisoners.
idiomatic: On xinsi a partial amnesty was granted to prisoners in the four prisons of Jinyang County, Taiyuan Commandery, Bing Province, and of the chancellor's office.

literal: Guim wei, Rouran sent envoys in court tribute.
idiomatic: On guim wei the Rouran sent envoys with tribute.
